discovery: Definitive measurement of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with the Planck satellite, establishing the precision standard cosmological model and evidence for primordial quantum fluctuations

nominees.name: Jean-Loup Puget
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Astrophysique Spatiale, CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay, France

nominees.name: George Efstathiou
nominees.affiliation: Kavli Institute for Cosmology, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom

motivation: Planck mapped the temperature and polarization anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background over the full sky to the cosmic-variance limit across the acoustic peaks. Its results fixed the content, geometry and age of the Universe to percent precision, demonstrated that a six-parameter LambdaCDM model describes the data, and measured a scalar spectral index significantly below one with near-Gaussian, adiabatic fluctuations - strong observational support for an inflationary origin of structure from quantum fluctuations. Planck also made the first high-significance all-sky reconstruction of CMB gravitational lensing and set leading bounds on neutrino masses, relativistic species and primordial gravitational waves. Puget and Mandolesi led the conception and construction of the High and Low Frequency Instruments, including the pioneering 0.1 K bolometer system; Efstathiou led the cosmological analysis and likelihood that made these results robust. Planck remains the benchmark against which fundamental physics in cosmology is tested.
